key_insight: The HOPE trial will test whether hypofractionated, dose-painted VMAT can reduce acute gastrointestinal toxicity while maintaining cancer control in stage I–IIB cervical cancer.
clinical_relevance: If effective, this approach could shorten treatment from 5 weeks to 4 weeks and potentially lessen early side effects for patients receiving concurrent chemoradiation.
method: 300 patients randomized 1:1 to experimental vs control arms
Experimental: 42.5 Gy/20 fractions to primary target and 36 Gy/20 fractions to pelvic nodes with weekly cisplatin 50 mg/m²
Control: 45 Gy/25 fractions to both target volumes with weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m²; both arms also receive image-guided brachytherapy
evidence_signal: This is a phase II randomized superiority trial designed to compare grade ≥2 gastrointestinal toxicity, with additional follow-up for 3-year disease-free survival, quality of life, and late toxicity.
watch_item: As a multi-center open-label trial, results may be influenced by differences in implementation across sites, and efficacy/safety will need confirmation before broad adoption.
paper_title: A phase II multi-center, open-label, randomized, parallel-group, superiority study to compare the acute toxicity of Hypofractionated dOse Painted External radiotherapy versus conventional external radiotherapy in patients with carcinoma cervix stage I - IIB. (HOPE)
